name: Work to earn

subjectOf.text: In a DAO, a member's influence and outcomes are determined by the value that member's contributions add to the shared work product, rather than by position in a hierarchy.
subjectOf.abstract: DAOs allow influence and outcomes of DAO members to be determined by the value a DAO member's contributions to the shared work product.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: contribution value is measurable and governs influence

subjectOf.text: High value contribution is self-amplifying in a DAO: when a member adds substantial value, other token holders want to add their skills to the same work product through a policing engagement, which focuses all members' joint efforts on the highest possible value proposition.
subjectOf.abstract: Moreover, if a DAO member adds substantial value to the DAO, other DAO token holders will want to add their skills to the same work product via a policing engagement which focuses all DAO members' joint efforts on the highest possible value proposition.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: members can observe and join high value work products

subjectOf.text: Work-to-earn DAOs must leave it entirely to each member how much time they contribute; DAOs that impose quotas and participation requirements may not be sustainable long-term in a value-to-efforts workflow environment.
subjectOf.abstract: In order to attract long-term talent, it needs to be always up to each individual DAO member how much time they put in. DAOs that create quota and participation requirements may not be sustainable long-term in a work-to-earn value-to-efforts workflow environment.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: work-to-earn DAOs seeking to attract long-term talent

subjectOf.text: Work to earn is the strongest of the six scored categories, yet it still averages only 4.9 out of 10 across the DAOs studied.
subjectOf.abstract: Based on the data in the graph above, the work to earn category scored much higher than all other DAO scorecard categories on average with a score of 4.9 out of 10.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Josh Bykowski, Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAO) – A Market Meta Analysis (2023). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4529715

subjectOf.text: The average Work to Earn score across the sampled DAOs is 4.1, ranging from 1 to 9, indicating only moderate effectiveness of contributor reward mechanisms across the market.
subjectOf.abstract: The average score across all DAOs is 4.1, with the highest score being 9 and the lowest score being 1.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Market Meta Analysis 2024 (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5254152
scope_conditions: work to earn scored on a 1 to 10 scale

subjectOf.text: A DAO that offers no paid work opportunities for participants stifles engagement, as scored for Hop DAO with a Work to Earn score of 1.
subjectOf.abstract: The DAO does not offer paid work opportunities for participants, stifling engagement (W: 1).
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Market Meta Analysis 2024 (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5254152
scope_conditions: DAOs with no compensated contribution channel
